clue.text: High-risk sport for those with a pressing need: rough, topless BMX Orienteering?

definitions.text: High-risk sport for those with a pressing need

indicators.note: roughed up, the letters are knocked into a new arrangement
the word BMX loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its head
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daredevil cross-country bike race is pitched as a thrill for people who badly need to get something done.
explanation.walkthrough: Extreme ironing is a real novelty sport: people press clothes on mountainsides, cliffs and riverbeds. 'A pressing need' is a pun on pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport's whole joke is doing household laundry chores in dangerous outdoor locations, hence high-risk.

clue.text: The main reason we won't join Europe on the level?

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, so this points to a stretch of water

definitions.text: reason we won't join Europe on the level
definitions.meaning: read politically it is British reluctance about the EU; read literally, water stops Britain physically joining the continent at ground level

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as political comment on Britain and the EU, but the reason is geographical: the sea between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: This strait is the body of sea separating Great Britain from mainland France and the rest of the continent.

clue.text: One madman turned up: leader of Conservatives, a shirty thing

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means these letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nut is slang for a crazy person

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A deranged figure turns up wearing a Tory leader's angry, shirty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shirty' usually means bad-tempered; here it just means shirt-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment like a long shirt, so it is jokingly a shirt-ish thing.

clue.text: Politician-speak makes you "evacuate gas"?

parts.note: to evacuate a space is to empty it
gas is informal for idle chatter

explanation.surface: A jibe that politicians' language is just a polite way of telling you to break wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuate gas' suggests flatulence; read as two words it gives an empty kind of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow promises and meaningless verbiage are what cynics expect from politicians' speeches.

clue.text: Sex is poor without painting up movie people

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters wrap round the others
the word is in poor shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then its letters are rearranged

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A grumble that sex scenes are weak unless film-makers add some artistic dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are the background actors hired in crowds for film scenes, so they are people in movies.

clue.text: See 1
One grand gets no small car to speak of — public disgrace!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the car's name is heard rather than spelt, so its sound is written down

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone with a thousand pounds still cannot afford a decent little car, which is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand (a thousand pounds) is slang. 'No mini' said aloud gives the ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is shame or dishonour suffered in the eyes of everyone.

clue.text: Love piece, visually stimulating work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a round shape
a part is a piece of something

explanation.surface: A romantic sculpture or painting that pleases the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is the 1960s movement of optical illusion paintings, made to stimulate the eye.

clue.text: Is Heather putting on weight in a capital place?

parts.note: taken as written
ling is another name for common heather
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman called Heather is gaining weight in some grand location.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of London, so it is a place in the UK capital.

clue.text: Gory countdown's screwed Bush's vision of USA?

indicators.note: screwed up, the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical swipe at a bloody war countdown, wrecking how President Bush sees America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue dates from 2004, the Iraq war period.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a land especially blessed by the Almighty, a view of America associated with George W. Bush's rhetoric.

clue.text: Find out soldier's not finished having an erection

indicators.note: the soldier's title is cut short to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a general is a high-ranking soldier
the cheeky sense of being up

explanation.surface: A soldier is caught out with an embarrassing state of arousal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is the standard abbreviation for General. To gen up, in British slang, is to research or get informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To gen up on something is to learn about it, an informal British phrase for getting the facts.

clue.text: Be inclined to grasp genitalia King put out like a squid

indicators.note: one word grasps, or holds, the other inside it

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be inclined to it

indicators.note: the King is put out, removed from the word

parts.note: tackle is British slang for a man's genitals

explanation.surface: A smutty instruction to grab someone's private parts while a monarch is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Squids have long grasping arms, so an animal with these limbs is described this way.

clue.text: Roving hand, one wanting a good greasing?

definitions.meaning: a wandering, groping hand, which seems to want touching
greasing a palm means bribing someone, so this hand craves payment

explanation.walkthrough: To grease someone's palm is to bribe them; a person with this hand is greedy for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a greedy, money-grabbing character, with a hand eager for bribes or cash.

clue.text: Series of steps taken to get Brown to resign

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to go is to quit a job

explanation.surface: A political manoeuvre to force Gordon Brown out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests the politician Gordon Brown, Chancellor at the time; it is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tango is a dance, made of a set sequence of moves and footwork.

clue.text: Politically correct in passion, so dated jazz lover

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: heat means intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: A politically correct person, passionately in love with old-fashioned jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepcat is old slang from the swing era for a hip fan of jazz music.

clue.text: Bogus identity rattled PM Tony used to get time off

indicators.note: shaken up, so the letters fall into a new order
the time letter is taken off before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Prime Minister Tony Blair is flustered over a fake identity he once used for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a false name adopted in place of one's real one.

clue.text: Still on top, Ursula initially (take good note) gets gobbled

indicators.note: only the first letter of Ursula is used

parts.note: only the initial letter of the name is used
NB, nota bene, is Latin for note well
something gobbled has been eaten

explanation.surface: A saucy scene of a woman called Ursula on top during oral sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A team undefeated so far is still leading, never having lost a game.

clue.text: Terribly unhip, me? Oh, you sound a brassy thing!

indicators.note: terribly suggests these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the exclamation becomes the letter O, which looks like it

indicators.note: the word you is spoken, giving the letter with the same sound

parts.note: said aloud, the word you is the name of a single letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being dreadfully uncool, and is told they are rather loud and brassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brassy' suggests a loud, brash person; here it is literal, an instrument in the brass family.
explanation.definitionFit: The euphonium is a tenor brass instrument, like a small tuba, common in brass bands.

clue.text: ""Point at which member dies off" was rather poetical

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a leg is a limb, or member

indicators.note: gone off, the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty definition of the moment a man's member goes limp.
explanation.definitionFit: To elegise is to write a mournful poem, an elegy, so the person was being poetic.

clue.text: Hickey involved with the French, in the dual manner of arses

definitions.text: in the dual manner of arses

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up together, so they combine and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A love bite on a French lover's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: A hickey is a love bite. The answer's root is cheek, slang for each half of a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttocks are cheeks, two of them, so acting with cheek is behaving like a bottom, impudently.

clue.text: See 1
To criticise one Conservative is to cause alarm

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to slate it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A warning that attacking a single Tory will spread fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic people is to throw them into sudden fear, so it means to alarm.

clue.text: See 8
Is able to walk arse over tip after cold drink

parts.note: C is the cold tap

indicators.note: head over heels, so the phrase is turned upside down and read backwards

parts.note: someone able to walk can go

explanation.surface: After a chilled drink, someone can barely stay upright and topples head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arse over tip' is British slang for tumbling head first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, an alcoholic spirit for sipping.

clue.text: A calling to account when car given to Tony's no.1

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: number one, the first letter of the name

parts.note: Tony Blair's name, of which only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Tony Blair faces questions after a car is given to him.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, which holds people to account.

clue.text: Murdoch title — highway robbery!

definitions.meaning: a newspaper owned by Rupert Murdoch, the press baron Private Eye loves to mock
an outrageous swindle, and also the literal crime of a robber on the road

explanation.walkthrough: A Private Eye jibe: the clue pretends to name a Murdoch paper and calls it robbery; the answer is the plain word for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Highway robbery is a classic form of stealing, so the general crime word covers it.

clue.text: Well done sticky stuff over one when gobbling date

indicators.note: the outer letters swallow the date letter whole

parts.note: goo is any sticky substance
on can mean over, as in a lid on a jar
you, like one, is the impersonal pronoun

explanation.surface: A sticky dessert poured over someone who is eating a date.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the abbreviation for date. 'Well done' looks like a cooking instruction for steak; it is praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheer of approval and congratulation, mostly Australian and British.

clue.text: One time sexual partner having erection in conference centre

indicators.note: in a down entry, erect letters stand upward, reading from the bottom

parts.note: a is one
lay is slang for a sexual partner

explanation.surface: A former lover becomes aroused at a conference venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One time' looks like 'former'; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta in Crimea hosted the 1945 summit of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.

clue.text: "On reflection, one's PR's awful," Brown's end as one out of political favour

indicators.note: the word on is reflected, so read backwards

parts.note: the clue's first word, taken as written before it is reflected

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: only the last letter of Brown is used

explanation.surface: A spin doctor admits poor publicity marks the end of Gordon Brown's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' seems to mean 'after thinking'; it reverses the word On.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-person is someone officially ignored or written out, especially by a political regime.

clue.text: A rock in the main? Gutless IDS a hindrance!

indicators.note: with its insides removed, only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the initials of Iain Duncan Smith, with the middle letter removed
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Calling the spineless Tory leader Iain Duncan Smith an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: IDS was Iain Duncan Smith, Conservative leader in 2004; 'gutless' mocks him. 'The main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a tiny island, a rock sticking up in the sea.

clue.text: Mediocre band of luvvies for which directors don't take full liability?

definitions.meaning: luvvies is mocking slang for theatre people

definitions.text: for which directors don't take full liability
definitions.meaning: a firm whose owners' liability for debts is legally capped

explanation.walkthrough: A company is also a troupe of actors, and limited can mean mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, this kind of firm protects its shareholders and directors from the business's debts beyond their stake.

clue.text: See 28
